title: Your Facility Was Priced for the Business You Were. Not the One You've Become.
linkedin:
Most business loan facilities are priced exactly once. At drawdown, the bank looks at your revenue, your margin, your security, your track record, and sets a rate. Then that pricing just sits there.

Here is what we see across owner-led businesses on the East Coast: revenue grows, debt gets paid down, the customer base diversifies, the interest cover ratio genuinely improves. None of that moves the rate on its own.

Banks are quick to reprice a business that has become riskier, a covenant test or annual review catches that fast. They are far slower to reprice one that has become safer. That direction only moves when the business, or someone acting for it, brings a clear comparison to the table.

The businesses this affects most are usually the ones doing everything right. A facility that was fairly priced three years ago quietly stays in place for the business that exists now, and nobody at the bank has a commercial reason to point that out.

An annual facility review closes that gap. Not a general opinion that things could be better, an actual comparison between the current structure and what the business's improved profile would support today.

Full piece on the ProfitPulse blog.

Quick one for business owners carrying a loan, overdraft or equipment facility that's more than a couple of years old.

Banks are diligent about repricing you if the business gets riskier. They are much slower to reprice you if the business gets safer, stronger revenue, lower debt, a longer track record. That direction only moves if someone actually asks.

When did you last actually compare your facility's terms to what your current numbers would support, rather than just keep paying what was set when it was signed?

A note for business owners across Brisbane, Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria carrying an existing bank loan, overdraft or equipment facility. Most of these get priced once, at the point the facility is first drawn down, based on the business's revenue, security and track record at that time. From then on, unless something forces a conversation, the pricing tends to just stay where it was set.

The trouble is the business rarely stays the same. Revenue grows, debt gets paid down, the customer base spreads out, and none of that improvement moves the rate automatically. Banks are usually quick to catch a business that has become riskier. They are far slower to notice one that has become safer, because that is not really their job once the facility is in place.

An annual review of existing facilities, checking the pricing, security and covenants against what the business's current financial profile would actually support, is one of the more overlooked habits available to a growing business. It costs nothing to ask the question, and the businesses that do tend to find real savings sitting in plain sight.

Read the full piece on the blog for what a proper facility review actually compares.
